terms.gloss: it is right, one should; what is expected
terms.grammar: verb, second conjugation, impersonal, with an infinitive or an accusative and infinitive
evidence: Plaut. Cas. 765–766: cēnam jam esse coctam oportuit
Ter. Heaut. 536: haec facta ab illō oportēbat
terms.comment: What was supposed to happen and did not: oportuit or oportēbat, in comedy often with a perfect passive infinitive (Plautus, Terence). “Not supposed to”, not allowed, is nōn licet (see allow).

terms.grammar: verb, second conjugation, with an infinitive
evidence: Plin. Ep. 8.16.5: plūra fortasse quam dēbuī
terms.comment: Of duty or obligation (Lewis & Short: classical prose uses it of moral necessity); for what had to happen of necessity, necesse est.

phrases.latin: quīn agitis hodiē? quīn datis, sī quid datis? properāte, cēnam jam esse coctam oportuit.
phrases.english: Come on, get moving! Hand it over, if you’re handing anything! Hurry: dinner was supposed to be ready by now.

phrases.latin: Haec facta ab illō oportēbat, Syre.
phrases.english: That is what he ought to have done, Syrus.

phrases.latin: nōn dēbēmus dēlicātī esse; ubīque medius caelus est
phrases.english: we mustn’t be fussy; the sky is the same everywhere

sources: Lewis & Short: oportet · Lewis & Short: debeo
